2607.09165.title: A Personalized Computational Framework for Assessing the Sufficiency of Partially Observed Data in Healthcare AI models
2607.09165.paper_summary: Achieving early and timely diagnosis and treatment for disease is a major challenge. Recent applications of machine learning (ML) algorithms trained on patient data have shown promise in many different settings for predicting the patient health state. A challenge often faced when applying these ML algorithms is that at any given time, not all clinical variables (features) needed as input to perform prediction tasks are available. We define the concept of full-feature-capacity (FFC) to refer to prediction performance when such algorithms make use of all features on which they were trained. We then introduce Feature Sufficiency Analysis (FSA) - an analysis for determining whether a subset of all clinical features needed by an AI model is sufficient to achieve FFC. FSA estimates the underlying distributions of missing variables conditioned on features that are available. FSA provides a patient-specific assessment of whether the existing set of measured features achieves FFC. If yes, then there is no need to acquire further inputs and a ML-based prediction. We provide two case studies: prediction of need for postoperative prolonged ventilation in patients recovering from heart surgery; 10-year mortality prediction in an outpatient cohort. We also demonstrate that FSA also provides a clinically interpretable feature-ranking methodology based on prediction sufficiency, identifies intrinsically hard-to-predict patient populations, and has the potential to perform cost-aware optimization for clinical data acquisition. FSA provides a generic computational approach for determining whether incomplete clinical information is sufficient to support trustworthy AI-assisted clinical decision-making, thereby facilitating the prospective deployment of healthcare AI systems across diverse clinical settings.
2607.09165.paper_summary_zh: 達成對疾病的早期及時診斷和治療是一個主要挑戰。最近在患者數據上訓練的機器學習（ML）算法的應用在許多不同的環境中顯示出預測患者健康狀態的潛力。應用這些ML算法時常面臨的一個挑戰是，在任何給定時間內，並非所有用於執行預測任務的臨床變數（特徵）都是可用的。我們定義全特徵能力（FFC）的概念，以指代這些算法在使用所有訓練過的特徵時的預測性能。接著，我們介紹特徵充分性分析（FSA）——一種分析，用於確定AI模型所需的所有臨床特徵的子集是否足以實現FFC。FSA估計缺失變數的潛在分佈，條件是可用的特徵。FSA提供了對現有測量特徵集是否達到FFC的患者特定評估。如果是，那麼就不需要獲取進一步的輸入，並且可以進行基於ML的預測。我們提供了兩個案例研究：預測心臟手術後患者需要延長通氣的情況；以及在門診隊列中的10年死亡率預測。我們還展示了FSA提供了一種基於預測充分性的臨床可解釋特徵排名方法，識別內在難以預測的患者群體，並具有進行成本意識優化臨床數據獲取的潛力。FSA提供了一種通用計算方法，用於確定不完整的臨床信息是否足以支持可信的AI輔助臨床決策，從而促進在多樣化臨床環境中前瞻性部署醫療AI系統。
